summary:
Round 2 of 2 for PR #2572 (efdf16dbf...9465eb048).

**Round-1 items**
- **Web dependency-cost suggestion: resolved as a documented tradeoff.** ADR-0094 and the investigation README now say only what is true. The web shell does not instantiate or render the native host. The shared code cost is recorded per route, in raw generated bytes, along with the 40→41 startup-budget control that argues against removing the import. Neither the 40-module web budget nor the 28-module native budget was loosened. Both builds at this head held them (40/40 web, 28/28 native). I accept the tradeoff.
- **320px native wrap (my round-1 unverified item): fixed, and I verified it independently.** I rebuilt `build:cap`, served it through `page.route` (no port, no network) and had the handler run `rival-probe/probe.mjs`. On `/privacy` and `/changelog`, in light and dark, all three sections sit on one row. Text is 14px, targets are 44px, the ExternalMark is present and nothing overflows. With idle prewarming disabled, a cold tap on the footer's Send feedback opens exactly one gate dialog and no popup.

**New since round 1**
I reviewed the 9465eb048 delta: the compact 160px reserve, the phone column gap, the new maximum-scroll guards and the documentation. The compact repair works at the three guarded sizes, and also at 932×430, 390×844 and 768×1024.

It does not cover desktop-width windows between 501px and about 614px tall, which are neither compact nor as tall as the 1280×800 guard. There the 96px reserve pushes the oldest changelog release out of its top-30% observer band at maximum scroll, so it never becomes active. The measured and modelled numbers are in the finding. Base keeps it active at those heights, so this is still a regression from the footer; it just falls outside the response's compact media query.

A browser-only control that sets the reserve to 160px at every size makes all 22 route/size combinations pass. The Privacy final section also stays active at every size (its top at most 24.5px, against a 128px spy line).

The probe scripts are kept in the worktree, as the handler asked: `rival-probe/probe.mjs`, `rival-probe/probe-fix.mjs`, and runnable copies in `web/`. I have not deleted them.

**Verdict:** one blocking finding. The fix is one CSS value plus a desktop-short guard.

findings.body:
**The response's tail repair misses desktop-width windows 501–614px tall: the oldest changelog release can never become active there.**

On changelog the spy band is the top 30% of the viewport (`rootMargin: 0 0 -70% 0`). `.history-end` reserves `70dvh − --page-footer-reserve`, and the footer's margin, box and page end follow it. So at maximum scroll the oldest release's bottom sits at about `0.3·H + R − (M + F + E)`. At desktop widths, M + F + E = 40 + 128 + 112 = 280px (M is the footer's margin, F its box height, E the sheet and page bottom padding; figures from the committed `tail-fixed.json` 1280×800 record).

With R = 96 that is `0.3·H − 184`, which is negative for any H below about 613px. Heights of 500px or less are rescued by the new `(max-height: 500px)` branch. Heights from 501px up to about 614px are not. Base had no footer, so its bottom was `0.3·H − 112`, which fits `tail-base.json` (127.86 at 800) and stays positive down to about 373px. So this is still a regression from the footer, one the three new guard sizes (1280×800, 320×568, 812×375) cannot see.

**Measured** in a fresh web build served via `page.route` (`rival-probe/probe.mjs`, run through the handler), at maximum scroll after hydration and `document.fonts.ready`:
- 1280×640: bottom 7.86, oldest active
- 1280×614: bottom −0.14, **not active**
- 1280×609: −1.14, not active
- 1366×600: −4.14, not active
- 1024×600: −4.14, not active
- 1280×560: −16.14, not active
- 1280×501: −34.14, not active
- 1280×500: 97.94, active (the 160px branch)

In every failing case the Changelog contents rail still reads `#release-1-6-0`. Viewports around 1280×600 are ordinary (a 1280×720 laptop screen minus the browser chrome), so a reader picking the oldest release from the rail lands with a different release named.

**Fix:** don't restrict 160px to compact layouts. Setting `--page-footer-reserve: 160px` on `.page` at every size, and dropping this media block, is safe in both directions:
- **Changelog:** 160px is still below the footer's real contribution at every measured size, so the oldest release's bottom stays inside the viewport.
- **Privacy:** its constraint is that what follows the last section must be at least 16 + R. That holds with room to spare: at least 212px follows it at 812×375, and 280px on desktop.

The browser-only control `rival-probe/probe-fix.mjs` injects just that override. Its maximum-scroll check (the same one as the new guard) passes on both routes at 1920×1080, 1280×800, 1280×614, 1366×600, 1024×600, 1280×501, 1280×500, 932×430, 812×375, 320×568 and 768×1024. The Privacy `#contact` top stays at or below 24.5px against the 128px spy line, and the footer stays in view. Also add `{ width: 1280, height: 600 }` to the viewport list in `page-footer.spec.ts`, so the gap between the compact branch and the 800px guard is covered.

unverified.claim: Base keeps the oldest changelog release active at desktop widths with heights of 501–614px. This comes from the linear model `0.3·H − 112`, calibrated against the committed `tail-base.json` (1280×800 bottom 127.86; the model gives 128). I did not build or measure base at those heights.
unverified.command: (not requested) build efdf16dbf and run rival-probe/probe.mjs against it
unverified.reason: I did not spend a final-round handler turn on it. The head measurements matched the same model's predicted threshold within 1px (predicted 613.3px; measured bottom −0.14 at 614px and 7.86 at 640px), so the conclusion does not depend on a base run.

unverified.claim: Every native-gate result (the one-row 320px footer and the single cold gate) comes from Chromium serving the static native bundle via `page.route`. None of it covers WKWebView/iOS, the Android WebView, or signed-app behaviour.
unverified.reason: Out of scope for this environment: there is no physical-device or signed-app rig, and the handler also makes no such claim.
